citations.quote: She has had a cough since July that will not go, and her doctor asked her straight away whether there was mould where she sleeps.
There is mould growing behind the wardrobe in our bedroom, and it is now spreading along the bedroom ceiling.
In addition, the boiler cuts out at night, so the bedrooms are cold in the morning.
I am not convinced and would like an expert to establish why the wall is damp before they just paint over it.
To be clear, I do not intend to withhold my rent or pay it into any deposit account; I have always paid on time and want to continue doing so.

plan.because: Needed to establish the parties, property and tenancy terms.
Needed to establish what defects were reported and when.
Needed to establish when the landlord received the report.
Needed to document the visible defects, locations and dates.
Needed to assess the response, proposed work and access arrangements.
The reported mould activates the moisture and temperature evidence branch.
The reported heating fault activates the service-report branch.
A persistent cough is reported; medical findings and any limits on attributed cause are relevant.
An expert assessment is sought and the cause of the damp remains open.
The customer expressly does not intend to use a rent deposit.
This is optional under the process.

questions: Is there an immediate health or safety concern requiring urgent assistance? Has the partner received medical advice about the persistent cough?
When did the mould and heating problems begin, and when and how were they reported to management?
What work or inspections have been proposed or carried out, and are any access arrangements pending?
Are dated photographs, temperature and humidity readings, a heating service report or a technical inspection available?
